dossier.claim: Complete English clauses repeatedly lose required words, use the wrong agreement, or confuse pronoun and verb forms. The intended event is often recoverable, but the sentence itself needs repair.
dossier.sourcePattern: Ordinary clauses, questions, and conditions with participants and relations recoverable from the Japanese. The examples include Rin’s condition for inheriting her father’s role, Saber’s orders, and Kirei’s comparison with Kiritsugu.
dossier.englishEffect: Missing subjects in “if wasn’t fun” and “if come any closer,” a missing second “as,” singular demeanor with “are,” and object “he and I” recur alongside malformed listening and breathing clauses. These are construction faults; they do not all change the plot.
dossier.limits: Conversational ellipsis, interrupted speech, literary fragments, nominative absolutes, and colloquial agreement are not automatically malformed. “Planning to” can omit an understood verb, and an unfamiliar expression is not necessarily ungrammatical. Spelling and word-sense faults may also support a separate dossier.
